newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Woolworth hits back at takeover critics.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth hits back at takeover critics.

text.p: F. W. Woolworth (Cyprus) on Thursday said its bid to take over the remaining 45 percent of novelty chain Zako Ltd was fair and it urged shareholders to consider its proposal.

The Cypriot company was responding to reports in the local media suggesting small shareholders in Zako were dissatisfied with the share for a share deal the boards of both companies agreed in early September.

The reports had suggested smaller shareholders did not consider Woolworth's bid generous enough, and also expressed discontent that a Zako rights issue planned for October was put on hold after the deal was announced.

Woolworth said its returns to shareholders from 1991 to September 1996 reached 19.2 percent annually, without including dividends for 1991 and 1992, while Zako showed returns of 12.1 percent, including dividends.
Woolworth, which has four department stores on the island, bought 55 percent of Zako share capital in February.
Zako has four main stores and 48 small outlets. It also has the franchise for the Next PLC clothing chain on the island. Its first shop is due to open in Nicosia on Friday.
Woolworth said Zako shareholders would be informed about the details of their bid in a prospectus due to be issued at the end of October.
